item.title: Forgot to log a period? How to repair the record in MiniCycle
item.description: Missed recording a period start in MiniCycle? Learn what happens to predictions, how to add the date later, and when not to guess.

item.title: Spotting between periods: what to note and when to get checked
item.description: A little blood outside your expected period can have many causes. Here is what spotting means, what to write down, and when to seek medical care.

item.title: Why the MiniCycle widget isn't updating, and how it refreshes
item.description: The MiniCycle home-screen widget updates on iOS's schedule, not the instant you log a period. Here is how WidgetKit refreshes it and what to check when it looks stale.

item.title: Ovulation pain (mittelschmerz): what that mid-cycle twinge is
item.description: One-sided pelvic pain can occur around ovulation, but timing and sensation cannot confirm the cause. Learn common features and signs that need medical assessment.

item.title: Why MiniCycle's predicted period date keeps changing
item.description: MiniCycle recalculates predictions from saved period starts, the cycle-length setting, and the current date. Learn which changes move the next expected period and what remains uncertain.

item.title: How long should a period last? What's a normal length
item.description: Several medical sources describe a typical period as lasting about 2 to 7 days. Learn about individual variation and bleeding changes that deserve medical advice.

item.title: Using MiniCycle's fertile window when trying to conceive
item.description: MiniCycle highlights seven dates from five days before estimated ovulation through the following day. Learn what that range means and why it cannot confirm fertility or ovulation.

item.title: Can you get pregnant on your period? What's actually possible
item.description: Pregnancy can result from sex during a period. Learn why ovulation timing is not fixed and why a calendar estimate should not be used as contraception.

item.title: What the MiniCycle statistics tab shows about your cycles
item.description: MiniCycle's statistics tab shows three summaries and recent cycle and period-length charts from the dates you recorded. Here is what the numbers actually use.

item.title: Period blood color: what brown, dark, and bright red mean
item.description: Period blood can appear bright red, dark red, or brown as flow and oxidation change. Learn why amount, duration, timing, and accompanying symptoms matter more than color alone.

item.title: Does MiniCycle work offline? Period tracking with no signal
item.description: MiniCycle's recording, prediction, and local-reminder features work offline. Firebase Analytics and optional iCloud Sync still require a connection.

item.title: PMS symptoms and timing: what's normal before a period
item.description: PMS involves physical or emotional symptoms that recur before menstruation and improve after it begins. Timing, severity, and effect on daily life all matter.

item.title: What data MiniCycle collects, and what stays on your phone
item.description: MiniCycle stores cycle records on the device by default, offers optional iCloud Sync, and uses Firebase Analytics for product-interaction measurement. Here is the current split.

item.title: What counts as a heavy period, and what's normal flow
item.description: Heavy menstrual bleeding is judged by duration, product changes, clots, disruption, and anemia symptoms rather than a home estimate of blood volume.

item.title: How to log a period start and end date in MiniCycle
item.description: Tap a date, pick period start, and MiniCycle fills the end with your period length. How logging start and end works, the seven-day replace rule, and the 14-day cap.

item.title: What to tell your doctor about your period: a tracking guide
item.description: Heading to a period appointment? What to track in the weeks before, which dates and symptoms are worth bringing, and how a clear record makes the visit faster.

item.title: How to add the MiniCycle widget to your iPhone home screen
item.description: Add MiniCycle's small widget to your iPhone home screen. It shows a four-week calendar around today using records and settings shared with the app.

item.title: Menstrual cramps: what's normal period pain, and what's not
item.description: Period pain is common, but pain that disrupts daily life or suddenly worsens should not be dismissed. Learn common patterns, relief options, and warning signs.

item.title: How to reset MiniCycle and erase all your period records
item.description: Reset records erases all period ranges, daily notes, and sexual-activity marks in MiniCycle. Learn what remains, how iCloud Sync reacts, and why it is not a backup.

item.title: How to start tracking your period: a beginner's guide
item.description: New to tracking? What to write down from day one, how a cycle is counted, why your first months of predictions stay rough, and the few changes worth a doctor's note.

item.title: Daily notes in MiniCycle: jot symptoms on any calendar day
item.description: Tap any date in MiniCycle to add a daily note: symptoms, flow, pain, mood, up to 999 characters. Notes stay on your device by default and never appear on the widget.

item.title: Perimenopause period changes: what's normal and what's not
item.description: Cycle intervals and bleeding can change during perimenopause. Learn what to record and which changes should be assessed by a clinician.

item.title: Hide sexual activity in your period tracker with Face ID
item.description: MiniCycle can hide sexual-activity marks from its calendar. Learn what the switch hides, why Face ID is required to show them again, and what the feature does not protect.

item.title: What counts as an irregular period, and when to see a doctor
item.description: Clinical sources use slightly different ranges for irregular cycles. Learn how to count cycle length, which changes deserve medical advice, and what a tracking app can document.

item.title: Auto vs manual cycle and period length in MiniCycle
item.description: MiniCycle can estimate your cycle and period length, or let you set them by hand (21–42 and 1–10 days). When auto fits, when manual fits, and why the estimate uses a median.

item.title: Ovulation signs and basal body temperature: the basics
item.description: Ovulation signs explained: the cervical fluid change before ovulation, the basal body temperature rise of about 0.3°C after it, and what ovulation tests show.

item.title: What each color means on the MiniCycle period calendar
item.description: What the MiniCycle calendar colors mean: solid pink records, striped expected periods, the sky-blue fertile window, and the small marks under each date.

item.title: What is a normal menstrual cycle length? It's a range
item.description: A 28-day cycle is a reference point, not a rule. Learn how major health sources describe typical ranges, variation, and changes worth discussing with a clinician.

item.title: How to edit or fix a wrong period date in MiniCycle
item.description: Logged a period on the wrong day? Learn how to edit period dates in MiniCycle: move a start, adjust an end, delete a record, and what happens to predictions.

item.title: The menstrual cycle phases: follicular, ovulation, luteal
item.description: The cycle is often described with menstruation, the follicular phase, ovulation, and the luteal phase, but menstruation overlaps the start of the follicular phase.

item.title: How to set up period, fertile-window, and ovulation reminders
item.description: Set local reminders for the expected period, fertile-window start and end, and estimated ovulation day. Most support 0–3 days of lead time; fertile-window end currently arrives on the estimated end date.

item.title: Why is my period late? What to check first
item.description: A late period can be related to pregnancy, stress, weight or exercise changes, illness, medication, or a health condition. Learn what to check and when to seek care.

item.title: How to keep your period tracker records when moving to a new iPhone
item.description: MiniCycle stores records locally by default and offers optional iCloud Sync. Learn what to check before moving to a new iPhone.
